binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω.
μ is equipped with the assumption that it is a probability measure.
X is a real-valued function on Ω.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Ω to the Borel measurable space on the real numbers.
conclusions: The lower Lebesgue integral over ω with respect to μ of the lower Lebesgue integral over positive real t of the indicator of t < X(ω) equals the same double integral with the t- and ω-integrations reversed.
mathematical_definitions: Let ν be real volume restricted to the open positive half-line (0, ∞).
Define F(ω,t) in ENNReal by F(ω,t) = 1 when t < X(ω), and F(ω,t) = 0 otherwise.
The asserted equality is ∫⁻_Ω (∫⁻_(0,∞) F(ω,t) dν(t)) dμ(ω) = ∫⁻_(0,∞) (∫⁻_Ω F(ω,t) dμ(ω)) dν(t).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable real random variable X on a probability space, integrating the nonnegative indicator that a positive level t lies below X(ω) first over levels and then over outcomes gives the same extended nonnegative value as integrating first over outcomes and then over levels.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The level variable t is integrated only over the strict positive half-line, so the integrand records the positive-level portion of X and does not include negative levels.
The inequality is strict: the indicator is 1 exactly when t < X(ω).
Both sides are ENNReal-valued lower integrals and may equal infinity; the statement does not assert finiteness or ordinary integrability.
No assumption that X is nonnegative, bounded, or integrable is present.
The probability-measure assumption restricts applicability, although the displayed nonnegative order-exchange equality itself resembles a result valid under more general measure hypotheses.
For choices of Ω and μ admitting no IsProbabilityMeasure instance, there is no applicable instantiation of the universally quantified statement.
ambiguities: Calling the result Fubini versus Tonelli is terminological; its ENNReal-valued nonnegative integrand makes the displayed claim Tonelli-type.
The mathematical reading treats the canonical real volume supplied by Real.measureSpace as Lebesgue volume.
